kind: Native read-only follow-up proposal; not a formal task receipt or implementation dispatch
coordinator_clarification: T08 is unstarted. The report ordering means after future T08 journal acceptance; no active task or completed T05C baseline is reopened. Upstream mode-preservation behavior is not established.

findings.message: The current-PM publisher does not preserve an existing story's Git executable class. atomic() always creates the replacement at 0600 (lines 95-100), and claimCurrentPm publishes the claimed story through that writer (lines 370-384). Its journal records and compares only text (lines 172-192, 208-231). This explains the observed 100755→100644 claim result and means normal publication and recovery have different, incomplete authority over file mode.

Transition publication preserves the live filesystem mode accidentally rather than proving the audited mode. atomic() copies the current target permissions (lines 88-105), but storyMode() constructs its comparison with the expected mode instead of reading the live mode (lines 208-215). The v1 journal and recovery bind only before/after text (lines 141-171, 381-393). A transition therefore inherits claim's normalized 0644 mode and can also accept and retain a later mode-only drift while recording the expected mode in execution_audit.

summary.scope: Preparation for a separate bounded correction after the active T08 journal work; no T05B, T02F or T08 scope change.
observed_evidence: The retained fixture ruling records a real executable story becoming Git 100644 during claim/transition and commit preparation refusing a later manual restoration to 100755.
The transition baseline already represents story entries as file:644|755:sha256, so mode preservation is part of the existing audited boundary rather than a new story-contract hash.
summary.upstream_evidence: The unchanged upstream project has no equivalent deterministic claim/transition writer. Its implementation-loop reference instructs the PM to append or update Execution and commit it. That supports preserving the story as a document, but it does not specify atomic replacement, journal recovery, or file-mode behavior. Any claim that upstream tooling preserves mode is therefore an inference, not verified parity.

minimal_future_correction.ordering: Start after T08 freezes its operation-specific current-PM journal format.
touches: tests/integration-correction.test.mjs only to cover the existing current-pm story-write call site
rules: Bind each existing story image as one text-plus-Git-mode pair; before and after use the same 644 or 755 class.
Before publication or recovery, require the live story to equal the exact before pair or exact after pair. Text from one image combined with another mode is a conflict and remains untouched.
Write the after image through an atomic replacement that retains the proven story mode. Keep journals, run records and newly created internal files at their existing 0600 policy.
Apply the same rule to ordinary claim, Execution transition, and their recovery paths. Audit the integration-correction story call site because it uses current-pm atomic(), without reopening T05C.

For transition-v1 recovery, derive the expected mode from the retained baseline/execution_audit. For legacy current-PM claim journals, use only mode evidence that T08 can uniquely derive from the tracked pre-claim story; otherwise refuse rather than reconstruct or normalize history.
Do not rewrite completed journals, runs, baselines or stories. Story contract/execution hashes remain byte-based, and counters retain their existing maxima.

acceptance: Claim and every legal transition preserve both 100644 and 100755 story modes while changing only the intended Execution bytes.
Fresh-process recovery at before-write, one-write and already-applied boundaries preserves the same mode and exact counters.
Mode-only drift and mixed text/mode states refuse without changing story, run, journal, hashes or counters.
A valid 100755 claim and transition reaches commit preparation without manual chmod; a real post-publication mode change remains detectable drift.
Legacy recovery makes no retrospective mode-proof claim where the old journal lacks sufficient evidence.
